conventions: Outcome keys are read from the convoy's side. 'win': the convoy earned the stage clear and beat the featured rival on track. 'loss': the featured rival won and the convoy did not earn the stage clear. 'clearedButLost': the featured rival won the race but the convoy still earned the stage clear (spec 5.2). The fourth case, where the convoy beat the rival on track but missed the benchmark, has no per-stage line: the results screen should explain it, and the featured rival's generic 'loss' line from rivals.story.json can be used. Speakers are rival IDs (Rxx), 'radio' (the Night Signal frequency voice), 'timing-crew' or 'narration'. Rivals may speak in scenes they are not racing in, as the story beats require. Stage lines address the driver or drivers as 'you', which reads correctly for one driver or six. The only placeholders are {player} and {convoy}. The 'diary' text is the race-diary entry that keeps the full story available after a shortened rematch intro.

acts.title: Learning the Frequency
acts.summary: A timing slip under a wiper brings the convoy to the Mizuhana tea roads and the Kasumi cedar forest. The Tea Hour Motor Club and Rainline Atelier teach that a controlled, repeatable run is worth more than a brave one. Daigo Ibuki gives the convoy a repaired aerial so it can hear the Night Signal properly, and the radio keeps changing the subject whenever an unrecorded dawn run over Amanagi comes up.

acts.title: Reading the Weather
acts.summary: Mist, rain and reservoir dawns show that uncertainty is not randomness. Emi Takanashi lends her weather notebook, and Reservoir Section insists on naming a reference point before chasing any number. In the Floodmark pump-house archive, Michi Kagawa finds an old carbon timing slip for the Amanagi dawn run with its final sector left blank.

acts.title: Between the Markers
acts.summary: On the Akebono coast and in the Hoshimi uplands the convoy meets bold harbour racers and the exacting Datum Works. It helps a timing crew, earns a place at a closed night event, and faces Jun Saegusa, who has to decide whether a perfect run is worth more than one that leaves options. The frequency keeps passing on small kindnesses from someone in an indigo coat who never gives her name.

acts.title: Before the First Train
acts.summary: Reina Kurogane, The Surveyor, recognises the old slip and won't say why, and a workshop argument reveals she once depended on a mentor she no longer names. In the Tsukishiro highland, Zero Frequency brings out a nearly silent radio recording and the restored dawn car. After Mako Hoshino's composure test and the Four Signals contracts, the convoy races Reina at Amanagi. On Hard it races Shiori Kuze, Zero Signal, at dawn.

normal.title: An Invitation, Not a Dare

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: A folded timing slip is tucked under your wiper: Tea Lantern Road, tonight. Bring whoever you trust.

intro.speaker: R01
intro.line: That's the invite! A slip, not a dare. Someone wants to see your times, not your nerve.

intro.speaker: R01
intro.line: We race here because the road's ours for an hour: lanterns up, deliveries not down yet. Seems a waste not to.

intro.speaker: timing-crew
intro.line: Closed from the tea-drying shed to the stone bridge. Marshals on the hairpin. Enjoy it.

intro.speaker: R01
intro.line: The hairpin before the flat is the whole lesson. A clean exit buys more than a brave entrance.

win.speaker: R01
win.line: You read that hairpin better than I did. I'll be thinking about it all through tomorrow's round.

loss.speaker: R01
loss.line: Close! The lanterns stay up all week. Come back tomorrow and I'll save you a cup.

clearedButLost.speaker: R01
clearedButLost.line: I got to the bridge first, but your time made the slip. That's the part the timing crew keeps.

normal.diary: The invitation came tucked under a wiper: a timing slip for Tea Lantern Road, not a challenge. Sora Matsuda explained that the tea-road crowd race because the road is theirs for one hour between lantern-lighting and the first deliveries. The lesson of the night was the hairpin before the flat finish: exit speed decides more than bravery on the way in.

hard.title: Dew on the Lantern Row

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Dawn, and the lanterns from last night are still lit. The road is damp from the tea fields.

intro.speaker: R05
intro.line: Sora gave you the friendly version. I'm the version that works the night shift.

intro.speaker: R05
intro.line: Damp road, so the exit is the whole race. Rush it, and you spend the flat watching my tail-lights.

intro.speaker: R01
intro.line: She's being kind. That's her kind voice.

intro.speaker: timing-crew
intro.line: Surface is damp and even from shed to bridge. Nothing hidden. Smooth hands.

win.speaker: R05
win.line: Neat exits. I'm writing that down, which is the highest compliment I own.

loss.speaker: R05
loss.line: There was room. Just not where you hoped. Try that exit a metre later.

clearedButLost.speaker: R05
clearedButLost.line: I kept the line and you kept the clock. Both of those go in my notebook.

hard.diary: Tea Lantern Road again, this time at dawn on a damp surface, with Yui Morisaki leading the Tea Hour grid. She defends the inside without ever swerving, so the only real way past was a better exit from the hairpin. Smooth hands mattered more than late braking.

normal.title: The Promise at the Turnout

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Blue hour over the terraced tea rows. Five hairpins up the switchback, and no two alike.

intro.speaker: R03
intro.line: A convoy is a promise to wait at the next turnout. That's the whole definition.

intro.speaker: R04
intro.line: Waiting is slow! No offence. Actually, a little offence.

intro.speaker: R02
intro.line: You're both right, which is annoying. Let's see whose version gets up the hill.

intro.speaker: R02
intro.line: Don't treat the hairpins as copies. Every pot on the wheel is a new pot.

win.speaker: R02
win.line: You drove that climb twice in your head before you drove it once. I could tell.

loss.speaker: R02
loss.line: I can do that fourth hairpin again, exactly the same. Come back and show me you can.

clearedButLost.speaker: R03
clearedButLost.line: Hanae won the climb, and you still made the time without leaving anyone behind. Toma owes me a tea.

normal.diary: On Mizuhana Switchback, Kei Naruse and Toma Fujii argued about what a convoy is: a promise to wait at the next turnout, or a reason to go slowly. Hanae Okuno settled it the way she settles most things, by driving the same entry into each of five different hairpins. Getting up the hill together turned out not to cost any time.

hard.title: Blue Hour, No Spare Seconds

intro.speaker: R06
intro.line: Evening. I'm the baker. No, that doesn't make me the easy one.

intro.speaker: R06
intro.line: The uphill target's tighter tonight. Each hairpin wants its own gear, like each loaf wants its own oven.

intro.speaker: R04
intro.line: He's been up since three baking. He's fine. He's always fine. It's terrifying.

intro.speaker: timing-crew
intro.line: Dry road, clear sky, tighter climb. The surface won't give anyone an excuse tonight.

win.speaker: R06
win.line: You found the crust by the split wall. Good. Most people only find the wall.

loss.speaker: R06
loss.line: Easy opponent, was I? The water tank doesn't care what you expected.

clearedButLost.speaker: R06
clearedButLost.line: I beat you to the tank, but your clock stayed honest. I'll take the race. You take the stage.

hard.diary: The blue-hour climb returned with a tighter uphill target and Akio Endo out in front. He reads rough transitions better than anyone in the Tea Hour club and hates being underestimated. Each hairpin needed a different gear and a different exit; copying one corner five times was not going to be quick enough.

normal.title: One Sector or One Lap

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Two laps past the canal sluice and the greenhouse frames. You'll brake for the raised bridge twice.

intro.speaker: R03
intro.line: Last week I set the best sector ever recorded on this loop. Also my worst lap. Same night.

intro.speaker: R07
intro.line: Kei framed the sector. I kept the lap chart. Mine is less flattering.

intro.speaker: R03
intro.line: One good sector is a map with one road on it. Show me two laps that agree with each other.

win.speaker: R03
win.line: Your second lap matched your first. That's rarer than a fast one. I'm annoyed and impressed.

loss.speaker: R03
loss.line: The map ends. The next bend doesn't. Try the bridge again with a gentler release.

clearedButLost.speaker: R07
clearedButLost.line: Kei took the race. You took the average. The lap chart likes you better.

normal.diary: Canal Orchard Ring brought out an old argument in the Tea Hour club: is a brilliant single sector worth more than a repeatable lap? Kei Naruse has the best sector on the board and a lap chart that Noa Ishida keeps showing to everyone. The raised-bridge braking zone came around twice, and it rewarded whoever braked the same way both times.

hard.title: Two Laps in the Dark

intro.speaker: R07
intro.line: Night loop, and I'm on the clock and in the car tonight. Very efficient. Terrible for my sleep.

intro.speaker: R07
intro.line: Lap one asks a question. Lap two answers it. If they disagree, I'll tell you. Loudly.

intro.speaker: R03
intro.line: They will. They said my packing-yard exit had the confidence of a wet napkin.

intro.speaker: timing-crew
intro.line: Night, dry, two laps, one clock. Tonight the second lap decides the target.

win.speaker: R07
win.line: Your laps rhymed. I checked twice. Best poem I've read all week.

loss.speaker: R07
loss.line: That was almost a sentence. Now say it again, same words, lap two.

clearedButLost.speaker: R07
clearedButLost.line: I won the race and you won the spreadsheet. I respect the spreadsheet more.

hard.diary: The orchard loop at night, with Noa Ishida driving and timekeeping at once. The target leaned on consistency: a quick first lap was worthless if the second lap drifted at the greenhouse offset. Noa links corners beautifully, but their rhythm breaks after one slow sector, so steady laps were the way to pressure them.

normal.title: The Cracked Cup

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: The bell workshop wheel turns beside the grid. Somebody has set out a folding table and a kettle.

intro.speaker: R04
intro.line: The double-apex right is flat. It's flat! Sora says it isn't flat.

intro.speaker: R01
intro.line: It's flat once. It's not flat twice. That's a different thing.

intro.speaker: R02
intro.line: Pass the lacquer. This cup cracked on the way up, and it'll still hold tea on the way down.

intro.speaker: R02
intro.line: Argue about the fast line all you like. The cup only matters if it comes back whole. Same for you.

intro.speaker: R04
intro.line: ...Okay. Fine. Come back whole. But fast.

win.speaker: R04
win.line: You braked later than me and still came back tidy. I need to stop apologising to my brakes.

loss.speaker: R04
loss.line: I got down first! And I didn't touch anything! Please don't tell Daigo how early I braked.

clearedButLost.speaker: R02
clearedButLost.line: Toma won the race, and you still made it back whole in time. Both cups are in one piece.

normal.diary: At the top of Bellmaker Descent, the Tea Hour club argued about whether the double-apex right by the workshops can be taken flat. Meanwhile Hanae Okuno mended a cracked cup with lacquer and pointed out that the fastest line means nothing unless you get back. Toma Fujii, who is still learning to trust his brakes, took that more to heart than he admitted.

hard.title: Bellmaker Before the Kettle

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Pre-dawn. The descent is damp and the workshop windows are still dark.

intro.speaker: R01
intro.line: The early vans come down here in an hour. We get it first. Damp, but ours.

intro.speaker: R01
intro.line: On the wet, the release is the brake. Let go too fast and the double-apex right lets go of you.

intro.speaker: R02
intro.line: The cup's mended, by the way. It's on the kettle table at the bottom. Arrive properly.

win.speaker: R01
win.line: You let go of the brake like you meant it. I hung on too long in the slow bit. Classic me.

loss.speaker: R01
loss.line: Beat you to the kettle! Sorry. I'll pour yours. Milk? No, it's green tea. Forget I asked.

clearedButLost.speaker: R01
clearedButLost.line: I won the sprint, you beat the clock. Hanae says that counts double before sunrise.

hard.diary: Bellmaker Descent in the damp before dawn, with Sora Matsuda leading and the early delivery vans due within the hour. Brake release was everything: the longer, softer release carried through the double-apex right, and the abrupt one did not. Hanae's mended cup was waiting on the kettle table at the bottom.

normal.title: Packed for Weather

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Rainline Atelier rolls in with folded tarps, a hygrometer and four thermos flasks. The sky is clear.

intro.speaker: R09
intro.line: Clear for now. The cedars are sweating, though. Listen to the tyres, not the forecast.

intro.speaker: R10
intro.line: She packed for rain. I packed to arrive on time. We both packed snacks.

intro.speaker: R09
intro.line: The road will stay dry tonight. I just like knowing why it stays dry.

intro.speaker: timing-crew
intro.line: Dry through all three esses. Reflectors cleaned this afternoon. The overlook's open.

win.speaker: R09
win.line: You drove the dry road as if you'd checked it yourself. Maybe you had. I'll stop assuming otherwise.

loss.speaker: R09
loss.line: The off-camber after the overlook needs a little patience. You'll find it on the next visit.

clearedButLost.speaker: R10
clearedButLost.line: Rika won the race, and you kept your promise to the clock. That's two kinds of on time.

normal.diary: Rainline Atelier arrived on Cedar Ribbon ready for weather that never came, and seemed quite happy about it. Rika Aonuma reads grip changes before anyone else notices them, and for the whole crew preparation is a personality, not a chore. The road stayed dry; the off-camber turn after the overlook still caught anyone who hurried it.

hard.title: The Patch by the Shelter

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Cedar Ribbon at night, and this time the damp is real. Rainline got here first again.

intro.speaker: R13
intro.line: That patch by the timber shelter wasn't there yesterday. It's there now. Drive what's there.

intro.speaker: R13
intro.line: There's more than one legal exit from those esses. Pick one you can repeat, not one off a poster.

intro.speaker: R09
intro.line: Fumio recut the drainage by the trestle this afternoon. He'll tell you it was nothing.

intro.speaker: R13
intro.line: It was nothing. Mind the reflectors.

win.speaker: R13
win.line: Good. You chose your own exit and kept it. No excuses needed, so I won't hear any.

loss.speaker: R13
loss.line: The damp caught you at the overlook. Don't blame the tyres. Tell me what you'll change.

clearedButLost.speaker: R13
clearedButLost.line: I beat you down the ribbon. Your clock's fine, though. Newcomers who listen get there.

hard.diary: Cedar Ribbon came back damp, with Fumio Senda leading: the forest-road maintainer who looks after newcomers and has no patience for excuses. Several legal exits from the rhythm esses were open, and the quick drivers chose one and repeated it. Fumio had recut the drainage by the rail trestle that afternoon and wouldn't talk about it.

normal.title: The Radio Changes the Subject

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: The access road below the shrine ridge. The old tram station is tonight's timing post.

intro.speaker: radio
intro.line: ...they say the Amanagi dawn run never went out on air. Nobody timed the end, or nobody will say. Anyway.

intro.speaker: radio
intro.line: The tram station urn is fixed. Thank you to whoever did that. Next: closures on the shrine approach.

intro.speaker: R10
intro.line: Did the radio just change the subject? It did. Everybody up here does that about the dawn run.

intro.speaker: R10
intro.line: Doesn't matter tonight. Long braking approach, then the zigzag. I'll be there first, and loudly.

win.speaker: R10
win.line: You set up the zigzag two corners early. That's my trick. Please give it back.

loss.speaker: R10
loss.line: Arrived first, as promised. There's tea on the plateau. Come up and tell me where it went wrong.

clearedButLost.speaker: R10
clearedButLost.line: I kept my promise to the finish and you kept yours to the clock. Nobody broke anything.

normal.diary: On the Shrine Approach access road, the roadside radio mentioned an unrecorded dawn run over Amanagi, then moved straight on to a repaired tea urn. Masato Kido says everyone in the hills changes the subject like that. His way up the zigzag is to set up two corners ahead, and anyone who planned only one was left behind.

hard.title: Dawn Below the Shrine Roof

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Dawn light on the distant shrine roof. The road is dry and the braking approach is long.

intro.speaker: R14
intro.line: I heard your downshifts from the tram station last night. We need to talk about third.

intro.speaker: R14
intro.line: There's less room for early braking this morning. Brake early and the engine sags out of its useful range.

intro.speaker: radio
intro.line: Morning, Shrine Approach. Clear skies. And no, we're still not discussing that other dawn.

intro.speaker: R14
intro.line: Nobody ever does. Listen to your engine instead. It's more honest.

win.speaker: R14
win.line: Clean shifts. Barely a stumble at the plateau. I'm almost disappointed I've nothing to mention.

loss.speaker: R14
loss.line: Your engine asked a question at the zigzag and you changed the subject. Try answering it.

clearedButLost.speaker: R14
clearedButLost.line: The race is mine and the clock is yours. Your fourth-hairpin downshift still made me wince.

hard.diary: Shrine Approach at clear dawn, led by Ena Kisaragi, a sound engineer who can hear a bad shift from the tram station. The Hard target left very little margin for early braking, so the long approach had to be used in full. The radio refused, cheerfully, to say anything more about the other dawn.

normal.title: Find Your Own Marker

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Bellmaker Descent again. The Tea Hour Motor Club has closed the whole road for its lieutenant.

intro.speaker: R08
intro.line: I'm not interested in your fastest run. I want the one you could do again tomorrow.

intro.speaker: R08
intro.line: Don't follow my brake lights down here. Find your own marker. Then find it again.

intro.speaker: R01
intro.line: He's giving the speech. It's a good speech. He gives it every time.

intro.speaker: R08
intro.line: It's a short speech. Get in the car.

win.speaker: R08
win.line: Repeatable. Controlled. Yours. That's the run I asked for.

win.speaker: R08
win.line: Take this aerial. I straightened it this afternoon. You'll hear the Night Signal properly now.

loss.speaker: R08
loss.line: Fast in places. Not repeatable. Come back when you can show me the same run twice.

clearedButLost.speaker: R08
clearedButLost.line: I won the descent, but you gave me the controlled run I asked for. Take the aerial. You've earned it.

normal.diary: Daigo Ibuki, the Tea Hour lieutenant, asked for one thing on Bellmaker Descent: a controlled run that could be repeated, not a lucky fast one. He brakes later and deeper than anyone on the mountain and warned against simply copying his brake lights. Afterwards he handed over a radio aerial he'd straightened himself, so the Night Signal would come through clearly from now on.

hard.title: The Mentor's Damp Descent

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Bellmaker again, damp from top to bottom. Daigo waits by the red footbridge with his brass stopwatch.

intro.speaker: R08
intro.line: Last time I asked for a repeatable run. Today the road asks the question for me.

intro.speaker: R08
intro.line: Brake later than feels comfortable, but controlled. Then take the exit wide on purpose. Not by accident.

intro.speaker: R08
intro.line: I'll know the difference. So will your tyres.

intro.speaker: R02
intro.line: He practised that speech on the kettle. Twice.

win.speaker: R08
win.line: Wide on purpose. Good. I spent twenty years teaching that, and you learnt it on a damp night.

loss.speaker: R08
loss.line: Those exits were wide by accident. Close. Not yet. I'll be at the footbridge.

clearedButLost.speaker: R08
clearedButLost.line: The stopwatch says the race is mine and the stage is yours. The stopwatch is rarely wrong.

hard.diary: Daigo Ibuki's Hard descent asked something new: brake later but stay controlled on a damp surface, then choose a wider exit deliberately. He watched from the red footbridge and could tell a planned wide exit from a slide that happened to end in the same place. The mentor had new words this time, and fewer of them.

normal.title: The Log Disagrees

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Mist lies low on the straights of Mistglass Hollow. The apexes stay clear and lit.

intro.speaker: R11
intro.line: Your diary says 'carry Cedar Ribbon speed'. The fog-mast log says the hollow runs six degrees colder.

intro.speaker: R13
intro.line: Read the mast, not the diary. The diary was written on a warmer night.

intro.speaker: R11
intro.line: Colder air, cooler tyres. Same road, different tempo. Count the woodland bends like phrases.

win.speaker: R11
win.line: You found the tempo in the fog! I lost count twice. Don't tell my teacher.

loss.speaker: R11
loss.line: Ha! I mean, well driven. Mostly. Your first woodland turn was a beat early.

clearedButLost.speaker: R11
clearedButLost.line: I won, but your time held. I rushed the aqueduct after my slide and you didn't. Hmph.

normal.diary: Advice copied from Cedar Ribbon said to carry the same speed into Mistglass Hollow. The fog-measuring mast's log said otherwise: the hollow runs colder, and cold tyres take longer to bite. Airi Shiba counts corners like musical phrases, and the tightening woodland sequence punished anyone who kept the old tempo.

hard.title: Damp Glass, Clear Apexes

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Controlled mist and a damp road. Apex lights along the woodland sequence stay readable.

intro.speaker: R15
intro.line: Fog makes people drive either timid or silly. Aim for neither.

intro.speaker: R15
intro.line: Use the old viewing platform as a sighting mark. It isn't a target, and neither is the edge.

intro.speaker: timing-crew
intro.line: Mist is controlled and apex visibility holds. If a marker fades, the marshals call it.

intro.speaker: R15
intro.line: Keep your margin. Or let me set the entry pace. I promise it's a very pleasant pace.

win.speaker: R15
win.line: You didn't let me set the pace. Good. I'd have made it far too comfortable.

loss.speaker: R15
loss.line: You braked for the fog, not the corner. Find the apex light, then trust it.

clearedButLost.speaker: R15
clearedButLost.line: I kept the margin and the lead; you kept the clock. Lovely night, all told.

hard.diary: Mistglass Hollow on Hard: controlled mist over a damp road, with every apex light still readable. Itsuki Hase is relaxed until the road gets narrow and exposed, then becomes very precise indeed. He will set a comfortable entry pace for anyone who lets him, so the way through was a firm but clean pace of your own.

normal.title: Uncertain Is Not Random

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Light rain on Rain Thread Pass. Water runs down the chains at the shelter.

intro.speaker: R16
intro.line: People call rain random. It isn't. It's uncertain, and that's a different thing entirely.

intro.speaker: R16
intro.line: Uncertain means you can still read it. Camber, drainage, the sheen by the yellow bridge. Look.

intro.speaker: R12
intro.line: I'll be out wide. There's a better angle from out here, especially in the wet.

intro.speaker: R12
intro.line: The waterfall at the tunnel exit sounds worse than it is. Don't brake for noise.

win.speaker: R12
win.line: You took the inside I left open. That's the price of a pretty angle. Usually worth it.

loss.speaker: R12
loss.line: Good pressure. But I had the picture framed from the tunnel mouth. Next time.

clearedButLost.speaker: R16
clearedButLost.line: Rui won the race. You read the surface well enough to earn the stage. That was reading, not luck.

normal.diary: Emi Takanashi, Rainline's lieutenant, turned up at Rain Thread Pass to make a single point: uncertainty is not randomness. Light rain was falling, but the camber, the drains and the sheen by the yellow bridge were all there to be read. Rui Takeda's wide wet entries leave the inside open on narrow roads, and that was the way past.

hard.title: Steady Rain, Honest Grip

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Steady rain now. The road is wet from the shelter to the long drainage descent.

intro.speaker: R09
intro.line: The reference time was set in this rain, on this road. No guesswork in it.

intro.speaker: R09
intro.line: The outside arcs on the cambers are predictable tonight, and predictable is fast in the wet.

intro.speaker: R16
intro.line: Grip is lower everywhere, and exactly where you'd expect. Nothing is hidden. Read it.

intro.speaker: R09
intro.line: Listen to the tyres. They talk more in the rain.

win.speaker: R09
win.line: You trusted the outside arc. I had doubts until the yellow bridge. Lovely.

loss.speaker: R09
loss.line: The tunnel exit was drier than you thought. Mm. You'll hear it next time.

clearedButLost.speaker: R09
clearedButLost.line: The race went my way and the rain went yours. That's a fair split on a night like this.

hard.diary: Rain Thread Pass in steady rain, against a wet reference calibrated in the same conditions. Rika Aonuma's outside wet arcs are slow to look at and quick on the clock. The surface under the tunnel roof stayed drier than the road either side, and noticing that was worth more than any amount of courage.

normal.title: Name Your Reference Point

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Reservoir Section runs the dam crest. Flood-level markings glow on the spillway towers.

intro.speaker: R17
intro.line: Hi! Before we race: what's your reference point? Brake board, tower, fishway? Pick one!

intro.speaker: R18
intro.line: He means it. Nobody here chases a number until they know what it's measured from.

intro.speaker: R17
intro.line: The crosswind on the crest sounds nasty, but the road's steady. Make the current work for you.

win.speaker: R17
win.line: You picked the second tower and hit it every time. I saw. That's the right answer. Ugh.

loss.speaker: R17
loss.line: Your reference point wandered. Mine stayed on the fishway. That's all it was!

clearedButLost.speaker: R17
clearedButLost.line: I won, you qualified, and you named your reference first. Kaede's going to like you.

normal.diary: Reservoir Section met the convoy on the Spillway Run dam crest with one demand: name your reference point before you chase a number. Shun Minato, a dam electrician, uses long smooth arcs to save his heavy car's torque. The crosswind was loud but harmless; the braking past the spillway gates decided the race.

hard.title: Dawn Across the Joints

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Dawn on the dam crest, damp. Expansion joints cross the road as thin dark lines.

intro.speaker: R21
intro.line: Joints every forty metres. Cross them straight. Don't steer on them.

intro.speaker: R21
intro.line: I'll be close behind you. Not touching. Just close.

intro.speaker: R17
intro.line: She's a radio editor. She cuts anything that isn't useful. Small talk included.

intro.speaker: R21
intro.line: Correct.

win.speaker: R21
win.line: You didn't look back once. That's how you get rid of me.

loss.speaker: R21
loss.line: You checked your mirror twice at the gates. That was the race.

clearedButLost.speaker: R21
clearedButLost.line: Race to me, clock to you. You still checked your mirror at the fishway.

hard.diary: Spillway Run at dawn, damp, with the dam's expansion joints to cross cleanly. Natsumi Hori follows closely without ever making contact and simply waits for a mistake. The drivers who ignored her in the mirror and drove their own line across the joints came out ahead.

normal.title: The Pencil Rolls Downhill

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: At the powerhouse, a map is spread over a bonnet. A mechanical pencil rolls off the edge.

intro.speaker: R18
intro.line: Ah. See? It rolled. The map's flat and the road isn't. Three hundred and sixty metres of climb.

intro.speaker: R18
intro.line: You drew your line with your elbow. On a climb, the apex moves when the hill does.

intro.speaker: R19
intro.line: She's been waiting all week for a pencil to roll. It's her favourite demonstration.

intro.speaker: R18
intro.line: It's an excellent demonstration.

win.speaker: R18
win.line: You moved every apex for the climb. That was drafting, not guessing. Well done.

loss.speaker: R18
loss.line: Close, but you drew the shelf road with a ruler. It bends. Gently. Look again.

clearedButLost.speaker: R18
clearedButLost.line: My line won, and your time still stands up to inspection. I'll sign that off.

normal.diary: A pencil rolling off a map at the Hydroline powerhouse gave Kaede Ueno the chance she'd been waiting for: on a long climb, elevation moves the apex. She places apexes with a draughtsman's precision but struggles when a bend changes radius. Planning for the hill, not the flat map, was what made the climb work.

hard.title: Tired Hands on the Hydroline

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Clear night on the Hydroline. Dry, with cold air sliding down under the pipeline arch.

intro.speaker: R22
intro.line: Hah! You're back! Good. Now do it when your hands are tired.

intro.speaker: R22
intro.line: Tonight's all gears and exits. Five and a half kilometres of them. Every hairpin wants a proper exit.

intro.speaker: R18
intro.line: Kenta has exited these hairpins about a thousand times. He's also brought lunch.

intro.speaker: R22
intro.line: Rice balls for after. Only if you exit the cable station properly.

win.speaker: R22
win.line: Ha! Those exits were better than mine! I'm eating your rice ball out of respect.

loss.speaker: R22
loss.line: You braked too long before the pipeline arch. I heard it from here. Next time!

clearedButLost.speaker: R22
clearedButLost.line: I won the climb and you kept the clock. Rice balls for everyone, then. Those are the rules.

hard.diary: The Hydroline Climb on a clear, dry night, led by Kenta Omi, a maintenance supervisor with a long memory and a very loud laugh. The Hard target rewarded gear choice and exits over the whole long ascent. Kenta's hairpin exits are excellent, but his braking distances can be beaten, and that was the opening.

normal.title: The Slip in the Pump House

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Dawn at Floodmark Circuit. Damp steps run down to the water past the twin pump houses.

intro.speaker: R19
intro.line: Look what was in the pump-house archive. A timing slip. Amanagi Dawnline. Very old.

intro.speaker: R19
intro.line: Four sectors filled in. The last one's blank. Not crossed out. Just... never written.

intro.speaker: timing-crew
intro.line: That's our old carbon format. We haven't printed those in years.

intro.speaker: R19
intro.line: I love old mistakes; they make good warnings. I don't think this one's a mistake, though.

intro.speaker: R19
intro.line: Anyway! Two laps. I know every mistake on this circuit, and they all end well.

win.speaker: R19
win.line: You never needed a recovery. That's the one thing I can't archive. Well driven.

loss.speaker: R19
loss.line: I slid at the stair and caught it. I know that mistake. It ends well, for me, tonight.

clearedButLost.speaker: R19
clearedButLost.line: I won, but your laps held. Keep this copy of the slip, by the way. I made two.

normal.diary: Michi Kagawa found an old carbon timing slip in the Floodmark pump-house archive: the Amanagi Dawnline, four sectors timed and the fifth left completely blank. It was the first solid evidence of the dawn run the radio keeps avoiding. Michi then won or lost on their usual talent, recovering quickly from a slide, which is exciting to watch and occasionally unnecessary.

hard.title: Floodmark in the Rain

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Night and steady rain at Floodmark. The water-level stair is running with it.

intro.speaker: R23
intro.line: Two laps, wet. The wide line only works when it comes back.

intro.speaker: R23
intro.line: Consistency matters more than bravery tonight. And caution isn't fear. Don't mix them up in front of me.

intro.speaker: R19
intro.line: She's in a good mood. That was nearly a paragraph.

intro.speaker: R19
intro.line: I've still got the old slip. The last sector's still blank, and nobody here will say why.

win.speaker: R23
win.line: Both laps agreed. Good.

loss.speaker: R23
loss.line: Lap two ran wide at the tank and didn't come back.

clearedButLost.speaker: R23
clearedButLost.line: Race to me. Stage to you. Your second lap was the one worth keeping.

hard.diary: Floodmark Circuit at night in the wet, with the stress on matching both laps. Sae Tsukada carries speed on wide, opening arcs and loses time when a radius tightens. The service tank corner does exactly that. Michi still carries the old slip with its blank last sector, and nobody at the Reservoir will explain it.

normal.title: Not a Good Accident

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Blackwater Hairpins: a long ladder of switchbacks down to the blue tunnel marker.

intro.speaker: R24
intro.line: Someone set a fast time here last week by sliding off the ladder and back on. Fast. Not good.

intro.speaker: R24
intro.line: I won't call an accident a good run. Show me control, and the clock can follow.

intro.speaker: R20
intro.line: Watch my release on the ladder. Not the turn. The release.

win.speaker: R20
win.line: Clean release. Good.

loss.speaker: R20
loss.line: Braking was fine. Release was early. Again.

clearedButLost.speaker: R24
clearedButLost.line: Ryo was faster. You were in control the whole way down. Both results are real.

normal.diary: Jun Saegusa, the Reservoir lieutenant, stood at the top of Blackwater Hairpins and refused to call last week's lucky fast slide a good run. The convoy had to show control on the asymmetric hairpin ladder. Ryo Senba, a machinist of very few words, rotates his mid-engine car beautifully but needs a clean brake release on downhill entries.

hard.title: The Ladder Before Dawn

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Pre-dawn on Blackwater, damp. Every hairpin marker is lit and in plain sight.

intro.speaker: timing-crew
intro.line: No fog, no surprises. Just damp. Every marker's where you last saw it.

intro.speaker: R17
intro.line: I'm usually impatient. Not on the ladder. The ladder needs patience or it takes yours.

intro.speaker: R17
intro.line: Heavy car, damp road. I'm slow changing direction. Use that. Legally.

win.speaker: R17
win.line: You caught me between hairpins. The heavy car hates that. So do I! Well done.

loss.speaker: R17
loss.line: Made the current work for me down the ladder. Your hands got busy in the tunnel.

clearedButLost.speaker: R17
clearedButLost.line: My race, your stage. Jun will want to see your trace. They always want the trace.

hard.diary: Blackwater Hairpins before dawn on a damp surface, with no loss of visibility anywhere: every marker lit and every corner where it was last time. Shun Minato's heavy car flows through long arcs but changes direction slowly. Short, legal attacks between hairpins were the answer.

normal.title: A Notebook, Not a Sermon

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Back on Rain Thread Pass in light rain. Rainline's lieutenant is waiting at the shelter.

intro.speaker: R16
intro.line: Last time here, you assumed the tunnel exit would be wetter than the bridge. Why?

intro.speaker: R16
intro.line: It wasn't. The tunnel keeps rain off the first forty metres. That assumption cost you.

intro.speaker: R16
intro.line: The rain isn't against you. It's information. Let's see what you do with it.

intro.speaker: R09
intro.line: She's been looking forward to this. The notebook was out at breakfast.

win.speaker: R16
win.line: Well read. Here's my weather notebook for this pass. It's more useful than a trophy.

win.speaker: R16
win.line: The pages on the drainage descent are the good ones. I'd like it back eventually.

loss.speaker: R16
loss.line: You were still driving last week's rain. Tonight's was different. Come back and read it again.

clearedButLost.speaker: R16
clearedButLost.line: I finished first; you finished informed. Take the notebook anyway. You earned the reading.

normal.diary: Emi Takanashi raced the convoy on Rain Thread Pass and began by questioning an assumption from the previous rain stage: that the tunnel exit must be wetter than the bridge. It wasn't. Instead of a victory speech she handed over her weather notebook for the pass, with its best pages on the drainage-side descent.

hard.title: Steady Rain, Long Lines

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Rain Thread Pass in steady rain. The whole road is wet and the drains are working hard.

intro.speaker: R16
intro.line: The safe line is longer tonight. It's also quicker, if you manage traction instead of fighting it.

intro.speaker: R16
intro.line: No secret grip anywhere. The benchmark was set in this exact rain. It's sharp, not unfair.

intro.speaker: R16
intro.line: Last time I lent you a notebook. This time I'd like you to add a page to it.

intro.speaker: R13
intro.line: Drains are clear. I checked them myself at six. You're welcome.

win.speaker: R16
win.line: That's a page worth adding. Your traction at the tunnel exit: write it down before you forget.

loss.speaker: R16
loss.line: You shortened the line when the rain got loud. The long line was the answer. Listen past the noise.

clearedButLost.speaker: R16
clearedButLost.line: I had the race; you had the rain worked out. Honestly, I'd rather have your page than my trophy.

hard.diary: Emi's Hard test on Rain Thread Pass came in steady rain: longer safe lines and a sharper traction-management benchmark, with no secret grip anywhere. Fumio Senda had cleared the drains himself that morning. Emi asked the convoy to add a page to her notebook rather than take one out of it.

normal.title: Harbour Voices

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Sunset over the sea viaduct. The lighthouse beam sweeps across the rust-red truss.

intro.speaker: radio
intro.line: Evening, Akebono! Ferry's in, fish is on ice, and the viaduct's closed for racing. Somebody make some noise.

intro.speaker: R25
intro.line: Welcome to the coast! Up in the hills they talk in decimals. Down here we talk in waves.

intro.speaker: R25
intro.line: Bold line on the cliff arcs? Please do. Just keep it on the tarmac and inside the rules.

intro.speaker: R26
intro.line: He's hospitable in the garage. On the viaduct he's someone else. Just so you know.

win.speaker: R25
win.line: Now that was a coastal line! Legal and loud. Come to the garage and I'll put the kettle on.

loss.speaker: R25
loss.line: The long way can still be the quick way! The port chicane just needs a bit more patience.

clearedButLost.speaker: R25
clearedButLost.line: I won, you qualified, and the lighthouse saw all of it. Good evening all round.

normal.diary: After weeks of reservoirs and rain notebooks, Breakwater Union met the convoy on Saltwind Viaduct with harbour gossip on the radio and a sunset behind the truss. Hiroto Namioka made it clear that bold lines are welcome as long as they are legal. He is superb through fast sweeping arcs and restless in the slow port chicane.

hard.title: Blue Hour at the Truss

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Blue hour on the viaduct. Dry and calm, with the coast railway running below.

intro.speaker: R29
intro.line: Ah. Good evening. There's still time to do the corner properly.

intro.speaker: R29
intro.line: The long arcs are tighter on exit tonight. Very little room to... ah... tidy up afterwards.

intro.speaker: R25
intro.line: He'll finish that sentence by the finish line. You won't.

intro.speaker: R29
intro.line: I will finish it. Eventually.

win.speaker: R29
win.line: You were patient through the arcs. That's... rarer than being fast. Thank you.

loss.speaker: R29
loss.line: You hurried the last arc, I think. There was still time. There usually is.

clearedButLost.speaker: R29
clearedButLost.line: I arrived first. You arrived within the timetable. We are both, ah, on schedule.

hard.diary: Saltwind Viaduct at blue hour with tighter exits from the long arcs, led by Seiji Tanabe, the night dispatcher nobody can hurry. He finishes clean however the surface changes, but gives away top-end aggression. Patience through the cliff arcs, followed by a committed exit, was worth more than bravado.

normal.title: The Poster Tells the Truth

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Fishmarket Midnight. The shutters are down, and a fresh poster is pasted by the tiled freight office.

intro.speaker: R26
intro.line: Like it? Your cars on the left, mine on the right. I drew you braking early. Artistic licence.

intro.speaker: R31
intro.line: Under yours you wrote 'they value patience'. Under hers: 'she values being watched'.

intro.speaker: R26
intro.line: ...I didn't mean to paint the honest bit that big.

intro.speaker: R26
intro.line: Doesn't matter. The quay turn is square. I left you a space. Not the one you chose.

win.speaker: R26
win.line: Fine. The overtake looked inevitable. For you. I'll redraw the poster.

loss.speaker: R26
loss.line: You went for the gap I painted. Everyone does. It's a very good painting.

clearedButLost.speaker: R26
clearedButLost.line: I kept position and you kept pace. The poster's going to need a second panel.

normal.diary: Maya Kuroda turned the rivalry into a poster for Fishmarket Midnight and, without meaning to, lettered each side's real values under the pictures: patience on one side, an audience on the other. She defends the inside assertively and legally, but a long defence costs her front grip. The square quay-side turn is where that shows.

hard.title: Market at Dawn

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Dawn at the fish market, damp. The quay braking zone shines beneath the crane silhouettes.

intro.speaker: R30
intro.line: Morning! Warmed up? No? Fine. You can be brave after you're accurate.

intro.speaker: R30
intro.line: Damp quay, square turn. Measured braking, not heroic braking. I'll brake later. I've trained for it.

intro.speaker: R26
intro.line: She did forty push-ups by the freight office. As a warm-up for talking.

win.speaker: R30
win.line: Yes! Accurate and brave. Great session. Same time next week?

loss.speaker: R30
loss.line: Good effort! Your braking was brave, not accurate. Accurate first. Again!

clearedButLost.speaker: R30
clearedButLost.line: I won the sprint and you hit your numbers. That's a proper workout. Stretch after.

hard.diary: The fish market at dawn on a damp surface, with the stress on measured braking at the quay. Akane Furuya brakes later than anyone on the coast and does it well, but she can be baited into the wrong exit gear. Accuracy first, then bravery: her own advice turned out to be the way to beat her.

normal.title: A Small Problem at the Ferry

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Tide Lantern Coast, early night. The storm gate is shut and the sea wall is damp.

intro.speaker: timing-crew
intro.line: Our beam receiver at the ferry terminal keeps missing cars. Anybody good with a reflector?

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Ten minutes of careful realignment later, the next car through reads perfectly.

intro.speaker: timing-crew
intro.line: Fixed! Right: tonight's event is invitation only. Consider yourselves invited.

intro.speaker: R27
intro.line: Ha! They let you in! That gate's been shut to me for a month for being 'loud on the radio'.

intro.speaker: R27
intro.line: Three late apexes by the inlet. Every gear is a choice. Make it a good one.

win.speaker: R27
win.line: HA! Look at that exit! You made the gear a good one! Oh, I'm furious. Wonderful.

loss.speaker: R27
loss.line: Boost bit you at the inlet, eh? Ha! Happens to me every week. Patience on the throttle.

clearedButLost.speaker: timing-crew
clearedButLost.line: Renji took the race. Your time's good for the stage, and the receiver's still reading clean. Thanks.

normal.diary: The timing crew on Tide Lantern Coast had a beam receiver at the ferry terminal that kept missing cars, and the convoy spent ten minutes realigning its reflector. That earned an invitation to the closed night event. Renji Sudo, a boat repairer with a laugh like a foghorn, uses torque and ratios cleverly, but his boost punishes a rushed exit from the late-apex corners by the inlet.

hard.title: Wet Wall, Lit Ferry

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Rain on Tide Lantern Coast. Along the sea wall, the wet sections give way to drier ones at marked points.

intro.speaker: timing-crew
intro.line: Surface transitions are marked with reflectors. Same for everyone, every time. We checked twice.

intro.speaker: R31
intro.line: I'll stay close through the undulations. No contact. Just company you'll notice.

intro.speaker: R31
intro.line: When the surface changes, you'll want to hurry. That's usually when I pass.

win.speaker: R31
win.line: You didn't hurry at the transitions, so I never got my opening. Well played.

loss.speaker: R31
loss.line: There. You hurried at the storm gate. That was all I needed.

clearedButLost.speaker: R31
clearedButLost.line: I passed you and you kept your clock. We were both patient, in different directions.

hard.diary: Tide Lantern Coast at night in the wet, with authored surface transitions marked by reflectors and identical for every car. Yori Kamei, a ceramic sign painter, applies patient pressure and passes cleanly when a rival hurries. On a short straight Yori rarely attacks, so the transitions were the only real danger.

normal.title: Who Checks the Board First

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Breakwater Ascent: harbour lamps below, the ridge radio dish above, and a funicular in between.

intro.speaker: R28
intro.line: I practised this climb forty times. So if it looks easy, that's the forty times talking.

intro.speaker: R32
intro.line: I'm not racing tonight, I'm watching. Don't perform for me. I'll know.

intro.speaker: R28
intro.line: She says that, then critiques everybody's hands for an hour.

intro.speaker: R32
intro.line: Only the interesting hands.

win.speaker: R28
win.line: Okay, that cliff zigzag was clean. You practised. Don't let anybody call you a natural.

loss.speaker: R28
loss.line: It took practice to make that look easy. It'll take you some too. That's fine. That's good, actually.

clearedButLost.speaker: R32
clearedButLost.line: Koharu won. But I watched the board, and you checked everyone else's result before your own.

normal.diary: Mako Hoshino sat out Breakwater Ascent to watch, and what she noticed was not lap times: she noticed who checked their friends' results before their own. Koharu Akiyama, a dancer who hates being called naturally gifted, links drifts smoothly up the cliff zigzag. She hesitates at isolated late-braking hairpins, though, and the climb has several.

hard.title: Harbour Before Sunrise

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Pre-dawn and dry. The breakwater lamps are fading as the harbour wakes up.

intro.speaker: R25
intro.line: Steep zigzag, then the high road. Too much torque on the cliff and the car just shrugs.

intro.speaker: R25
intro.line: Save it for the top. The high road's where the long way turns into the quick way.

intro.speaker: R32
intro.line: Still watching. Hiroto gets impatient in the slow bits. Just an observation.

intro.speaker: R25
intro.line: She's right. Please don't use that.

win.speaker: R25
win.line: You used it! Of course you did. Great torque management, though. Truly.

loss.speaker: R25
loss.line: Got you on the high road! Held back on the cliff, let it go at the top. That's the trick.

clearedButLost.speaker: R25
clearedButLost.line: Race to me, stage to you. Mako's writing something down. That's never nothing.

hard.diary: Breakwater Ascent before sunrise, dry, with the emphasis on torque management up the cliff zigzag. Hiroto Namioka flies on the broad high road but gets impatient in slow compound corners, and Mako pointed that out to everyone. Holding torque back on the cliff and releasing it at the top was the whole climb.

normal.title: Three Decimal Places

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Slatecut Service Road. The surveyor hut above the quarry has its lights on. Datum Works has arrived.

intro.speaker: R33
intro.line: Your printout: every braking point, every apex speed, three decimal places. Compliments of Datum Works.

intro.speaker: R39
intro.line: We'll call it a success if you match our reference on all three rock-cut bends. Only then.

intro.speaker: R33
intro.line: Luck doesn't interest me. Show me something you could repeat, and then we'll talk.

win.speaker: R33
win.line: Repeatable. I'll want to see it again, of course. That isn't doubt. That's method.

loss.speaker: R33
loss.line: My sectors matched my reference. Yours wandered. Numbers aren't cruel. They're patient.

clearedButLost.speaker: R39
clearedButLost.line: You met the stage target. By our definition, that isn't success yet. By the timing crew's, it is.

normal.diary: Datum Works arrived at Slatecut Service Road with printouts to three decimal places and a very selective definition of success. Tetsu Arimura believes a repeated result is more interesting than a lucky one, and he drives like it. The timing crew's clear and Datum's idea of success turned out to be two different things.

hard.title: Dusk on the Shoulder

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Dusk, damp. The quarry's gravel shoulder is clearly bounded and the tarmac edge is sharp.

intro.speaker: R37
intro.line: Tea first. Genmaicha, a little cooler than you'd think. Then we race.

intro.speaker: R37
intro.line: Advice: stay off the gravel. Choose the gear that suits the bridge. That's it. That's all the advice.

intro.speaker: R33
intro.line: He lectured on ratios for four hours this morning. That was the summary.

win.speaker: R37
win.line: Right ratio, clean edges. Good. Your tea's gone cold, though. That's on you.

loss.speaker: R37
loss.line: The engine isn't tired. You chose the wrong ratio. Third before the bridge, next time.

clearedButLost.speaker: R37
clearedButLost.line: Race to me, stage to you. Now, a second cup. The water should be exactly right by now.

hard.diary: Slatecut at dusk on a damp surface, with clean boundaries between tarmac and gravel shoulder. Osamu Kitani, a veteran tuner with elaborate tea preferences, gave the simplest advice of the campaign: stay off the gravel and pick the right gear for the quarry bridge. His ratios are perfect for terrain he knows and less flexible when he's pushed off his planned rhythm.

normal.title: How Does It Feel

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Kilnlight Ring. Warm light in the kiln windows, cooler light across the cooling-tower ribs.

intro.speaker: R34
intro.line: Everyone asks me about power. Nobody asks what the car feels like when you sit in it. Why?

intro.speaker: R34
intro.line: I stitch seats. I can tell how a car will lean before it moves. Ask me that instead.

intro.speaker: R35
intro.line: She's not wrong. It's irritating, but she's not wrong.

intro.speaker: R34
intro.line: The seat is comfortable. Don't get comfortable.

win.speaker: R34
win.line: Your throttle in the cooling yard was clean. The car looked settled. I could see it from here.

loss.speaker: R34
loss.line: Too eager on entry. The car told you. You just weren't listening to the seat.

clearedButLost.speaker: R34
clearedButLost.line: I won, but you drove like you'd asked the car first. The clock agrees. Good.

normal.diary: At Kilnlight Ring, Chika Sakurai asked why everyone talks about power before they ask what a car feels like. She is an upholsterer who can read a car's balance from the seat. Her throttle is beautifully clean on exit, but she gives away entry speed, and the tight cooling-yard loop comes around twice.

hard.title: Different Faces at the Kiln

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Kilnlight at night, dry. Datum Works has sent a different set of drivers this time.

intro.speaker: R38
intro.line: New lineup! Nobody told you? We shuffled everyone. It's an experiment.

intro.speaker: R38
intro.line: The usual line was getting lonely. I'll show you three others. All legal. One of them is good.

intro.speaker: R34
intro.line: It's usually the second one.

win.speaker: R38
win.line: Beaten! That's still a result, which is still data. Filing it with my failed prototypes. Fondly.

loss.speaker: R38
loss.line: The alternate arc worked! Mostly. Once. Once is a start.

clearedButLost.speaker: R38
clearedButLost.line: I won with the strange line; you qualified with the sensible one. Science wins either way.

hard.diary: Kilnlight Ring on Hard, with a reshuffled Datum lineup led by Tsubasa Muraoka, an industrial designer who keeps every failed prototype. Tsubasa tries creative legal alternative arcs, and on the closing-radius corner under the bridge they sometimes experiment too far. A steady, ordinary line was the right response.

normal.title: A Run That Leaves Options

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Blackwater Hairpins again. Jun Saegusa has brought a caliper, a clipboard and the heavy sedan.

intro.speaker: R24
intro.line: My run here is technically perfect: same apex, same speed, every hairpin. You've seen it.

intro.speaker: R24
intro.line: A perfect run leaves no options. If something changes, it breaks. I've never needed options.

intro.speaker: R24
intro.line: Measure twice. Brake once. Then show me whether your run can bend without breaking.

intro.speaker: R22
intro.line: They practise in front of a mirror. With the caliper.

win.speaker: R24
win.line: You kept your options open and still beat the line. I don't like it. I respect it more than I expected.

win.speaker: R24
win.line: Mine was perfect. Yours was useful. I'll have to decide which I'd rather own.

loss.speaker: R24
loss.line: Your run had options. It also had errors. Remove the errors, keep the options.

clearedButLost.speaker: R24
clearedButLost.line: The measurements say I won. The stage says you're ready. Both measurements are correct.

normal.diary: Jun Saegusa, the Reservoir lieutenant, brought their technically perfect Blackwater run to compare with a run that leaves options open. Jun's line is so consistent that a patient rival can see exactly where it will go and wait for the opening. The respect the convoy earned wasn't the kind Jun usually gives, and it was more useful.

hard.title: Cold Blackwater, Changed Numbers

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Cold and damp on Blackwater. Jun has changed the car's setup, legally. They checked twice.

intro.speaker: R24
intro.line: I assumed the perfect line would hold in any weather. It doesn't. I measured it.

intro.speaker: R24
intro.line: New brake-release pattern tonight. Longer. Softer. I had to rebuild my own habit to find it.

intro.speaker: R24
intro.line: I'm saying this aloud because it was hard to write down: I was wrong about something.

intro.speaker: R18
intro.line: I've known Jun eleven years. That's the first time I've heard that sentence.

win.speaker: R24
win.line: You adapted faster than I did. I needed a notebook and a week. Noted, with respect.

loss.speaker: R24
loss.line: The new release works. It took me a month to admit I needed it. You'll need less.

clearedButLost.speaker: R24
clearedButLost.line: I won with a line I'd have called wrong last season. You earned the stage. Things change.

hard.diary: On cold, damp Blackwater, Jun Saegusa arrived with a new, fully legal setup and an altered brake-release pattern, and admitted out loud that an old assumption had been wrong. Kaede Ueno had apparently never heard Jun say that before. The longer, softer release was the key to the hairpin ladder in these conditions.

normal.title: She Knows the Slip

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Switchyard Skyline. Power lines crown the ridge and the service lift glows at the overlook.

intro.speaker: R35
intro.line: Naturally aspirated tonight, of course. Power is useful. Wasting it is expensive.

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: A white-and-graphite coat passes the timing table and stops at the old slip pinned there.

intro.speaker: R40
intro.line: Old carbon format. Nobody prints these any more. Good luck tonight.

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: She puts it down very carefully, squares it to the table's edge, and walks on.

intro.speaker: R35
intro.line: That was Reina Kurogane. She doesn't stop for anything. She stopped for that.

win.speaker: R35
win.line: You wasted less than I did. That's the only compliment I give, and I mean it.

loss.speaker: R35
loss.line: You spent too much on the arcs and had nothing left for the climb. Budget, not bravado.

clearedButLost.speaker: R35
clearedButLost.line: I took the race; you took the stage. And Reina's still looking at that old slip. Curious.

normal.diary: Reina Kurogane, The Surveyor, appeared at Switchyard Skyline only briefly. She stopped at the old Amanagi slip on the timing table, called it an old format, and set it down with far more care than that remark deserved. Naozumi Fuda, meanwhile, drove the power-line arcs with his usual efficiency and his usual caution in a crowded opening sector.

hard.title: Composure After Compression

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Pre-dawn and damp on Switchyard Skyline. The descending arcs compress hard beside the pylons.

intro.speaker: R39
intro.line: The compressions unsettle drivers. Not cars. Drivers.

intro.speaker: R39
intro.line: I'll be right behind you after the pylons. If you start watching me, I've already won.

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: At the timing table, the old slip has gone. A careful photocopy has been left in its place.

win.speaker: R39
win.line: You stopped watching me after the first compression. Unusual. Good.

loss.speaker: R39
loss.line: You were quicker before you started watching me. Again.

clearedButLost.speaker: R39
clearedButLost.line: Race to me. Your composure held for the stage. For accuracy, I'll note one wobble at the lift.

hard.diary: Switchyard Skyline before dawn, damp, where the test was composure after each compression beside the pylons. Ayame Sugiura sits close without contact and waits for an error, but a driver who ignores her mirror presence simply outpaces her. At some point in the night the original slip disappeared from the timing table, and a neat photocopy was left in its place.

normal.title: Argument in the Machine Hall

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: The restored machine hall at the foot of Ember Quarry Drop. Datum Works is arguing again.

intro.speaker: R33
intro.line: Reina's line is perfect and repeatable. That's the whole argument.

intro.speaker: R36
intro.line: She didn't learn it alone, Tetsu. She used to ride down here in someone's little roadster. Every week.

intro.speaker: R33
intro.line: ...She's never mentioned that.

intro.speaker: R36
intro.line: No. She stopped mentioning it. Right, argument translated: everybody, get in your cars.

win.speaker: R36
win.line: You avoided every mistake I'd have recovered from. Tidier than me. Annoyingly.

loss.speaker: R36
loss.line: That's recoverable. Your pride may take longer. I'll put the kettle on in the hall.

clearedButLost.speaker: R36
clearedButLost.line: I won and you qualified. Now, nobody tell Reina what I said in the machine hall. Please.

normal.diary: A Datum Works argument in the restored machine hall let something slip: Reina Kurogane didn't learn her line alone. Lina Hayase remembers her riding down the quarry road every week in somebody's small roadster, and Reina has never mentioned that person since. Lina recovers from mistakes brilliantly, and sometimes relies on that instead of avoiding the mistake in the first place.

hard.title: Wet Drop, Narrow Envelope

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Night rain on Ember Quarry Drop. The recovery zones are broad, but the safe braking envelope is tighter.

intro.speaker: R33
intro.line: Wet reference, measured tonight. Brake inside the envelope and you'll be fine. Outside it, you won't.

intro.speaker: R36
intro.line: Tetsu. Say the other thing.

intro.speaker: R33
intro.line: ...Lina says Reina learnt the lattice-bridge braking from someone else. I've filed that as evidence.

win.speaker: R33
win.line: Three braking zones, three matches. That's evidence. I'm going to think about it quietly.

loss.speaker: R33
loss.line: One good braking zone is a story. You braked outside the envelope twice. That's a pattern.

clearedButLost.speaker: R33
clearedButLost.line: Race to me, stage to you. Both results reproducible. That's all I ask.

hard.diary: Ember Quarry Drop in the wet with a tighter safe braking envelope, led by Tetsu Arimura, who wants three matching results before he believes one. His decisions become predictable under pressure. Before the start, Lina persuaded him to repeat what she knows: Reina learnt the lattice-bridge braking from a teacher she no longer names.

normal.title: Just a High Road

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Moonridge Contour. Moonlight on the ridge, the observatory dome far off, a cold dry road.

intro.speaker: R41
intro.line: Hi. Sorry. Okay. The high road. People tell stories about it. It's a road. It's a nice road.

intro.speaker: R41
intro.line: Open arcs, then the old snow shed. It's darker inside, but your lights are fine. Then the plateau S.

intro.speaker: R41
intro.line: There's no test up here. Nobody's watching from the pavilion. Just drive what you can see.

intro.speaker: R43
intro.line: She talks a lot beforehand. Wait until she's driving. Quiet as the observatory.

win.speaker: R41
win.line: Oh, that was lovely. You saw the exit. Sorry. I mean: well driven.

loss.speaker: R41
loss.line: I could see the exit. That was enough. Um. You'll see it too. Really.

clearedButLost.speaker: R41
clearedButLost.line: I got the race, you got the stage. So we both got home. That's the nice version.

normal.diary: Fuyu Tachibana, an observatory assistant who chatters nervously until she's behind the wheel, described Moonridge Contour plainly: open ridge arcs, a darker section through the old snow shed, and a quick plateau S. No legends, no tests, just a road. She is superb on narrow highland sections and overcautious in broad corners.

hard.title: Moonridge Before Light

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Pre-dawn on Moonridge. Cold air, dry road. Frost on the old snow fence, none on the tarmac.

intro.speaker: timing-crew
intro.line: Surface is dry, checked by sensor and on foot. No ice. The frost is scenery.

intro.speaker: R45
intro.line: I checked your tyre pressures. And your wheel nuts. Habit. Then I checked mine.

intro.speaker: R45
intro.line: The contour is long. Keep some of the car for the plateau.

win.speaker: R45
win.line: You had car left at the end. That's the whole trick. Most people don't believe it until they see it.

loss.speaker: R45
loss.line: You spent everything on the ridge arcs and the plateau collected. Save a bit next time.

clearedButLost.speaker: R45
clearedButLost.line: I finished first; you finished strong. Your car's in good shape. I looked.

hard.diary: Moonridge Contour before dawn, dry, with frost on the scenery and none on the road; the timing crew walked it to be sure. Minae Otsuka, a former endurance mechanic, checked everyone's car before her own. Her low-waste lines rarely include a surprise attack, so a well-timed one on the plateau S was worth trying.

normal.title: What Isn't on the Tape

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: White Pine Descent at dawn. Kazuma Yorita sets an old receiver on the weather-station step.

intro.speaker: R42
intro.line: This is from the Amanagi relay. That morning. Listen.

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Hiss. An engine idling. A door. Then a long stretch of nothing.

intro.speaker: R42
intro.line: Hear what's missing? No gearchanges. No braking. Whoever that was, they'd stopped racing.

intro.speaker: R42
intro.line: I won't tell you more than I heard. Now then: the quiet part of this road is where you hear the car.

win.speaker: R42
win.line: You listened to the camber. Good. Keep listening. That's where the rest of the story is, too.

loss.speaker: R42
loss.line: You rushed the avalanche gallery. The rock face is cold; the road isn't. Hear the difference next time.

clearedButLost.speaker: R42
clearedButLost.line: I got down first. You got the stage, and you heard the recording properly. That matters more.

normal.diary: At the White Pine weather station, Kazuma Yorita played an old, almost silent recording from the Amanagi relay. What mattered was what wasn't there: no gearchanges, no braking, no finish. Just an idling engine and a door. Kazuma refuses to embellish anything, and on the long cambered descent he reads cold-road transitions better than anyone.

hard.title: Cold Pines, Published Setup

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Cold night on White Pine Descent, damp. The wet setup sheet is pinned at the weather station for everyone.

intro.speaker: R46
intro.line: Everyone gets the same setup sheet. I drove it at nine and checked it again at ten.

intro.speaker: R46
intro.line: Long braking into the triple bend. Release it the way a train settles at a platform.

intro.speaker: R46
intro.line: Oh. That joke from the pine grove earlier. It was funny. I'll explain it later.

win.speaker: R46
win.line: Smooth release. You'd have made a fine driver on the mountain line. That's a compliment from my era.

loss.speaker: R46
loss.line: Early at the gallery, late at the finish. Ha. That's the joke, you see. On time is a kind of fast.

clearedButLost.speaker: R46
clearedButLost.line: I arrived first and we both arrived on time. The timetable balances. Lovely.

hard.diary: White Pine Descent on a cold, damp night, with a published wet setup available to every entrant. Gaku Nishio, a retired train driver, brakes with extraordinary smoothness, though his modest power means every exit has to be perfect. His jokes arrive late. His braking never does.

normal.title: The Dawn Car

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: At the transmitter service building below Signal Tower Climb, a cover slides off a small cream roadster.

intro.speaker: R47
intro.line: The car from the dawn run. Kogane Kestrel S. Restored, not replaced. Every part I could save, I saved.

intro.speaker: R48
intro.line: Excuse me. What were the tyres reading after the last climb? The left rear, particularly.

intro.speaker: R47
intro.line: Oh. Um. Four degrees cool, left rear.

intro.speaker: R48
intro.line: Thank you. That's fine. Good luck, everyone.

intro.speaker: R43
intro.line: Who was that? ...Never mind. Leave yourself a road home tonight. The ridge approach is quick.

win.speaker: R43
win.line: Ha! You flowed through the ridge and still stopped at the markers. Both. Good.

loss.speaker: R43
loss.line: The steep middle ate your flow. Leave yourself a road home, then use all of it.

clearedButLost.speaker: R43
clearedButLost.line: I got home first; you got home in time. Everyone home. Best possible result.

normal.diary: Yuna Senzaki unveiled the restored dawn car at the foot of Signal Tower Climb: a cream Kogane Kestrel S, repaired rather than replaced. A quiet woman in a worn indigo coat asked about its left-rear tyre temperature, thanked her, and wished everyone luck. Then Neri Takase led the climb, flowing along the ridge and, unusually for a fast driver, respecting every marked braking zone.

hard.title: First Light on the Tower

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: First light on Signal Tower Climb. Dry. The beacon mast still blinks against a pale sky.

intro.speaker: R47
intro.line: The final sector is steep. Momentum is everything. Lose it there and the climb won't give it back.

intro.speaker: R47
intro.line: I'm racing tonight. Not in the dawn car. It isn't mine to race. In my own.

intro.speaker: R48
intro.line: Your left rear will be cool at the start again. Give it one corner.

intro.speaker: R47
intro.line: ...She's watching. Okay. Old doesn't mean finished. Neither do I.

win.speaker: R47
win.line: You carried more speed through the steep sector than I did. I tried too hard. I know.

loss.speaker: R47
loss.line: I linked it! The last sector! With her watching! Okay. Okay. Good race.

clearedButLost.speaker: R47
clearedButLost.line: I won the climb and you kept the clock. And she nodded. At both of us, I think.

hard.diary: Signal Tower Climb at first light, dry, where the Hard target depended on momentum through the steep final sector. Yuna Senzaki raced in her own car rather than the restored Kestrel, and tried a little too hard with the legend watching. Shiori Kuze gave her one piece of advice about a cool left-rear tyre, and it was correct.

normal.title: Four Beacons Lit

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Four Signals Traverse. For the first time this season, all four coloured marshal beacons are lit.

intro.speaker: R44
intro.line: Four beacons, four ways to lose speed: the entry, the arcs, the descent, the high road.

intro.speaker: R44
intro.line: And four ways to keep it. The marker is there for a reason. Then there's your reason.

intro.speaker: timing-crew
intro.line: Tonight's a regular race. The beacons are for reading. The old timing cabin's open for tea.

intro.speaker: R44
intro.line: I remember every apprentice who drove this badly. I'd rather not remember you.

win.speaker: R44
win.line: You kept your flow on the high road. That's my weak sector, and you found it. I'll remember that.

loss.speaker: R44
loss.line: You braked well on the descent, then lost it all on the high road. Flow, not just stopping.

clearedButLost.speaker: R44
clearedButLost.line: I won, and you learnt all four beacons. Next time they'll mean more. You'll see.

normal.diary: All four coloured marshal beacons were lit on Four Signals Traverse, each marking a different way to lose or keep momentum. Satoshi Mibe, a snow-shed technician with blunt manners and a perfect memory for apprentices, brakes superbly on the descent but loses flow over long gentle sections. The smooth high-road finish was where he could be caught.

hard.title: Four Beacons at Dawn

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Dawn on Four Signals, dry. The four beacons glow pale against the sky.

intro.speaker: R41
intro.line: Every sector's judged more tightly this morning. That's... sorry. That's not scary. It's just precise.

intro.speaker: R41
intro.line: The technical entry is narrow, and I like narrow. The high road's broad. I'm less good at broad.

intro.speaker: R44
intro.line: She's just told you her weakness. Mountain manners. Don't waste it.

win.speaker: R41
win.line: You were quick on the broad parts. I was too careful. I know, I know.

loss.speaker: R41
loss.line: I could see the exit every time. The beacons helped. Sorry. I mean, thank you for the race.

clearedButLost.speaker: R41
clearedButLost.line: My race, your stage. All four beacons. I'm actually really pleased for you.

hard.diary: Four Signals at dawn, with every sector assessed more tightly. Fuyu Tachibana is precise on the narrow technical entry and too cautious on the broad high road, and she said so herself before the start. Satoshi called that mountain manners.

normal.title: When Everyone Is Watching

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Ember Quarry Drop at night. Every crew on the Night Signal has come to watch the fourth lieutenant.

intro.speaker: R32
intro.line: Big crowd! Lovely. Lights, lattice bridge, and everybody's favourite cape.

intro.speaker: R32
intro.line: ...All right. No cape voice. Honest question: can you stay composed with everyone watching?

intro.speaker: R32
intro.line: I couldn't, once. So I learnt to perform instead. It worked. It was also a hiding place.

intro.speaker: R32
intro.line: Show me the line you'd choose without an audience. I'll try to do the same.

win.speaker: R32
win.line: Composed, with the whole mountain watching. That's harder than winning. Take both.

win.speaker: R32
win.line: Reina will be at Amanagi. She'll ask the same question without any warmth. You're ready for it.

loss.speaker: R32
loss.line: You drove for the crowd at the lattice bridge. I know that line. I invented that line.

clearedButLost.speaker: R32
clearedButLost.line: The race is mine, but you stayed composed. The crowd saw it. More importantly, I did.

normal.diary: Mako Hoshino, Breakwater's fourth lieutenant and a former champion, dropped the performance at Ember Quarry Drop and asked a plain question: can you stay composed when everyone is watching? She admitted that her bravado started as a hiding place. Her combined-corner rotation is bold and controlled, but she will sometimes overrotate for style and give away the next straight.

hard.title: Wet Drop, No Cape

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Rain on Ember Quarry Drop. Mako is in the car without the cape, and the crowd is quieter.

intro.speaker: R32
intro.line: No showy rotation tonight. Wet quarry, restrained lines, strong exits. That's the whole plan.

intro.speaker: R32
intro.line: Someone once ran Amanagi at dawn with less power than anyone here, and never once looked hurried.

intro.speaker: R32
intro.line: Zero Signal. Shiori Kuze. She's real, she's still around, and she drives like this: nothing wasted.

intro.speaker: R32
intro.line: If you want to meet her on that road, show me you can keep speed without spending it.

win.speaker: R32
win.line: That's her way, near enough. Restraint that's still fast. Yuna should hear about this.

loss.speaker: R32
loss.line: You spent speed at the bridge. Shiori wouldn't have. I only just didn't. Again.

clearedButLost.speaker: R32
clearedButLost.line: My race. But your exits were the quiet kind. I'll tell Yuna you're worth her test.

hard.diary: On a wet Ember Quarry Drop, Mako Hoshino left the cape and the showy rotation behind and drove a restrained, exit-first race. Before the start she named the legend outright: Shiori Kuze, Zero Signal, who ran Amanagi at dawn with less power than anyone and wasted nothing. Keeping speed without spending it was Mako's condition for passing the convoy on to Yuna.

normal.title: Four Signals, Four Contracts

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Four Signals Traverse. One race, four sectors, four contracts. Reina's invitation depends on them.

intro.speaker: R39
intro.line: Entry: beat the published sector time and touch both apex gates. I'll be checking both.

intro.speaker: R37
intro.line: Arc: bank the drift target across the three marked corners. No circling back for points.

intro.speaker: R46
intro.line: Descent: no wall contact, no reset, and release the brakes inside the marked zone.

intro.speaker: R45
intro.line: Horizon: beat the posted exit-speed targets and the full-route time. Keep some car for it.

intro.speaker: R39
intro.line: Pass all four to qualify. Pass three, finish legally and in time, and you've supported. Clear?

win.speaker: R39
win.line: Four contracts, no inconsistencies. I looked. Reina's invitation is yours.

win.speaker: timing-crew
win.line: Contracts confirmed. Amanagi Dawnline is open to you. Reina has been told.

loss.speaker: R39
loss.line: A contract failed. The board shows which one. Practise that sector, then come back.

clearedButLost.speaker: R39
clearedButLost.line: I crossed the line first, but your contracts hold for the stage. Consistent. I checked twice.

normal.diary: Before Reina's final invitation could be accepted, the convoy had to pass the Four Signals test: one race, judged in four contracts. Entry demanded the sector time and both apex gates; Arc, the drift target across three marked corners; Descent, no wall contact or reset and a legal brake release; Horizon, the exit-speed targets and the full-route time. Ayame Sugiura inspected every result and found no inconsistencies to mention.

hard.title: Preserve the Car

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Four Signals, before dawn. Yuna Senzaki runs the test herself. Shiori waits at the old timing cabin.

intro.speaker: R47
intro.line: Same four contracts, tighter targets: Entry, Arc, Descent, Horizon. All legal, all published.

intro.speaker: R47
intro.line: What I care about: finish with a car that could do it all again. Don't spend it on the Arc.

intro.speaker: R47
intro.line: No wall on the Descent, and a clean brake release. On the Horizon, keep speed without abusing it.

intro.speaker: R48
intro.line: If they look after the car, I'll race them. If not, there's no hurry. There never is.

intro.speaker: R47
intro.line: All four to qualify; three plus a legal finish in the envelope to support. Go gently. Go fast.

win.speaker: R47
win.line: All four, and the car still feels sweet. She's walking to the Kestrel already. That means yes.

win.speaker: R48
win.line: Thank you. At dawn, then, at Amanagi. Bring the same car you finished with.

loss.speaker: R47
loss.line: You used the car up on the Arc. The board shows which contract broke. Rest, then try again.

clearedButLost.speaker: R47
clearedButLost.line: I crossed first, but you looked after the car and your contracts held. Shiori says yes.

hard.diary: Yuna Senzaki ran the Four Signals test on Hard with tighter legal targets and one extra thing to care about: finish with a car that could do it all again. Shiori Kuze watched from the old timing cabin and made her condition simple: look after the car and she would race. The Arc was the temptation. Drivers who spent their tyres there had nothing left for the Horizon.

normal.title: One Driver at a Time

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Amanagi Dawnline. A ridge launch in the dark, a horizon sweep through the tunnels, sunrise over the sea.

intro.speaker: R40
intro.line: You came as a convoy. You'll still reach every corner one driver at a time.

intro.speaker: R40
intro.line: I trust a perfect line because it can't let me down. People can. I learnt that on this road.

intro.speaker: R40
intro.line: Prove me wrong on the road, not in speeches. Past the relay arch, over the valley bridge, into the sunrise.

intro.speaker: R34
intro.line: She's nervous. You can tell, because she's being extremely polite.

intro.speaker: R40
intro.line: I'm being precise, Chika. Grid, please.

win.speaker: R40
win.line: My line was perfect. Yours was shared, and still every bit your own. I didn't expect that.

win.speaker: R40
win.line: ...Come up to the terrace. I think I owe a few people a conversation.

loss.speaker: R40
loss.line: The line held. It always does. Come back when your convoy can hold one too.

clearedButLost.speaker: R40
clearedButLost.line: I finished first and you earned the clear together. I'm beginning to think those are different questions.

normal.diary: Reina Kurogane, The Surveyor, raced the convoy on Amanagi Dawnline, from the dark ridge launch to the sunrise finish above the sea. She believes a perfect line is the only thing that can't let you down, and she drove one. Her weakness is commitment to the ideal line when the road asks for a different rhythm, and a convoy that shares a result without losing its individual skill was a rhythm she hadn't planned for.

hard.title: The Dawn Run

intro.speaker: narration
intro.line: Amanagi Dawnline. Mist lies in the valley, lifting slowly. The cream Kestrel idles at the relay arch.

intro.speaker: R48
intro.line: Good morning. The car is legal, the tune is published, and the mist will clear on schedule.

intro.speaker: R48
intro.line: Years ago I stopped at this arch. I don't regret it. Today I'd like to finish.

intro.speaker: R48
intro.line: You don't have to hurry every part of the road. Only the parts that deserve it.

intro.speaker: R47
intro.line: Her tyres are warm. I checked. Then she checked after me. Good luck.

win.speaker: R48
win.line: Thank you. The whole road, used properly. I don't mind at all that it was yours.

win.speaker: R48
win.line: Come to the terrace later. There's a slip I've been meaning to finish.

loss.speaker: R48
loss.line: Thank you. You hurried the bridge, that's all. The sun will come up again tomorrow.

clearedButLost.speaker: R48
clearedButLost.line: I crossed first. You earned your clear without wasting a thing. That's the run I hoped to see.

hard.diary: Shiori Kuze raced Amanagi at dawn in her restored Kogane Kestrel S, legal in every respect, with a published tune and mist clearing on a fixed schedule. She preserves speed with minimal steering and a measured late release, and in her low-powered car any real loss of flow is expensive. She told the convoy she had stopped at the relay arch years ago and didn't regret it. This time she meant to finish.
